findings.claimed: curves.ts:64 and vasculature-courses.ts:150-156 both claim their record type is "a structural superset of `TractRecord`"; SceneLayers.tsx:805/822/839 mounts `<TractTube>` with a TractRecord, a NerveCourseRecord and a VesselCourseRecord respectively.

findings.subject: consistency · the v18 `variant` prop duplicates information the record already carries (`kind`)
findings.claimed: TractTube.tsx:424-431 — the variant selects `createVesselMaterial` instead of `createTractMaterial`.
findings.expected: A kind-derived decision, the way the sibling pass already does it: `hintForKind(kind)` (NucleusMesh.tsx:67-79) maps `vessel → 'vasculature'` from the record's own kind, with the call site passing nothing.

The mount at SceneLayers.tsx:839/840 therefore passes a hand-written discriminant that must be repeated for every future vessel mount, and the tract/nerve mounts (SceneLayers.tsx:805/822) omit it. If `variant` is kept, add the missing gate assertion.

findings.subject: consistency · three near-identical course mounts in SceneLayers, two with the same inlined pairing rule
findings.claimed: Each block documents itself as "the same tube, the same gate, their OWN registry kind".
findings.expected: One mount helper parameterised by table + material family, or at minimum one shared pairing predicate.
findings.basis: Measured duplication: the tracts block and the nerves block contain the byte-identical expression `const paired = getTaxonomyEntry(x.id)?.laterality === 'paired'` (only the binding name differs: `tract.id` vs `course.id`); only the vessels block differs, calling `isPairedVessel(course, getTaxonomyEntry(course.id)?.laterality)`. findings.subject: consistency · the course-record hierarchy is three parallel definitions, not one hierarchy
findings.claimed: The brief asks whether `VesselCourseRecord` vs `NerveCourseRecord` vs `TractRecord` is "a coherent superset hierarchy or duplicated".
findings.expected: Either one base type with two extensions, or an explicit statement that the three are structurally compatible by design.
findings.basis: Measured: all three declare their own copies of `id`, `name`, `direction`, `modality`, `origin`, `target`, `decussation`, `function`, `waypoints`, `tubeRadius`, `color`, `levels?`, `synonyms?`, `clinical`, `refs` — 15 fields, ~18 lines re-declared twice (curves.ts:83-128 = 46 lines, vasculature-courses.ts:106-176 = 71 lines). Neither course type extends `TractRecord`; `VesselCourseRecord` extends only the new `VesselCourseHead` (the v8/v17-only fields: parent, surface, basis, elementIds, anchorNote, territory, supply, calibreMm). `TractRecord.tubeRadius` has no `calibreMm` sibling, so the mm↔au conversion rule (v14 §3.4) lives only on the two course types.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce `interface CourseRecordBase extends Omit<TractRecord,'somatotopy'|'synonyms'>` in src/types.ts and have both course types extend it, deleting the duplicated declarations. That makes the documented superset relation a compile-time fact and removes the drift surface (already visible in the `refs` optional/required difference). Costs one file outside this audit's write scope, so route it to the integrator only if the finding is accepted.
findings.notes: Judgment, not a defect: the duplication is documented, deliberate and type-checked at the call sites. It is filed because the brief asked for a verdict on the hierarchy, and "three parallel definitions with a prose superset claim" is the accurate answer.

findings.subject: consistency · hasVesselCourse() returns true for records that own no course

findings.subject: tech debt · the v12g --sidebar-w narrow-breakpoint gap is STILL OPEN (56 px) and no gate covers it

findings.expected: The header's first grid column tracks the sidebar column at every breakpoint where both exist.
